search_log: Searched: "Gothikana RuNyx excerpt first chapter publisher"; found and opened the Macmillan publisher excerpt.
Searched: "Gothikana RuNyx point of view third person narration" and "Gothikana third-person RuNyx"; found explicit completed-book descriptions of third-person POV.
Searched: "Gothikana RuNyx alternating POV third person" and "Gothikana POV Corvina Vad"; results described dual Corvina/Vad focalization but no sustained change of grammatical person.
Searched Google Books and authorized-sample variants; no useful Google Books preview was surfaced. A Penguin sample result was opened but proved to be a different RuNyx title and was discarded.
Opened a 14-page Nerd Daily excerpt PDF, but it duplicated the opening evidence available directly from Macmillan and was not treated as independent support.
Opened SuperSummary's Chapters 10-16 guide to check interior structure; its named Corvina and Vad chapters and quoted third-person wording corroborated the opening evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, principally focalized through Corvina with some Vad sections. Numerous interior Goodreads event passages describe Corvina and Vad as she/he while rendering their private perceptions, and the publisher's sustained opening independently uses the same third-person mode for both characters. Explicit whole-book reviews and an interior chapter guide corroborate that dual POV means alternating focal characters within third-person narration, not alternating narrative person. First- and second-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue and do not represent the base narrator. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found.
